_comment: Instantiation manifest for report-delivery-pipeline.json - deploy one Logic App per entry, fixing its parameters as below (scripts/build_logicapps.py derives build/logicapps/<name>/workflow.json from this file). Every pipeline enforces the same storage rule: Reports/<Supplier>/<Service>/ (Advisory/<Topic>/<Subtopic>/ for advisoryRoot), supplier folder reused if present, service folder created only when missing. Keys map 1:1 to workflow parameters: agent->agentName (the Agents v2 runtime addresses agents by NAME, finding C1) PLUS agentVersion, which build_logicapps.py reads from build/agent-versions.json so every pipeline pins `<agent>:<version>` and never runs 'latest' (finding C19; shared.verifierAgent resolves the same way into verifierAgentName/verifierAgentVersion), reportType, renderFormat, renderTemplate, libraryRoot->libraryRootItemId, approvalKind, shared.sensitivityLabel->sensitivityLabelId (finding C16; a per-report-type override comes from templates/registry.json `sensitivity_label`), supplierNameFallback, serviceNameFallback, portfolioStatusOnStore, appendScoreHistory (omitted = pipeline default). Bind apiVersion to the FOUNDRY_API_VERSION app setting (setup/.env, default v1 - the classic threads/runs surface 2025-05-01 is the documented fallback and retires 2027-03-31).

deepsearch-report.notes: Agent gathers public info via Bing grounding and Euronext tooling (SecurityScorecard, IAF, ENX gateway MCP - read-only; Defender Graph / Jira Assets CMDB only if attached in integrations/registry.json) and emits the finished single-file HTML dashboard per the V17.02.11 template with data-overall-score="NN" on <body> (agent addendum). The verified HTML is the source for the scheduled-deepsearch low-score Jira gate. NOTE: SharePoint serves .html as a download, not inline - see sharepoint/README.md.

dpia-dpo-report.notes: OT PDF uploaded by the user (inputFileIds). Stored under Reports/DPO/<Supplier>/<Service>/ and share link sent to the DPO channel.

cyber-forum-pptx.notes: Requirement c: OT PDF(s) -> Infosec Cyber Forum deck for CISOs/stakeholders. DECISION: the deck IS the verified 8-slide Group CISO Governance template (ciso-reporting); no separate Cyber Forum slide template exists in the export. Threat-intel context for the forum comes from the separate cyber-forum-brief pipeline (DOCX) attached alongside the deck - no merge of the two contracts (keeps the byte-verified template untouched). NAMING DECISION: the pipeline id stays `cyber-forum-pptx` and is NOT renamed to `ciso-governance-pptx` even though the deck is the Group CISO Governance template - the id is the join key of three files (templates/registry.json `ciso-reporting-deck`.pipelines, team/approval-policy.json REPORT_DELIVERY.pipelines, and build/logicapps/<id>/ which names the deployed Logic App), and it is the requirement-c label the users know (team/USER_QUICKSTART.md section c, agents/orchestrator_instructions.md row c). Renaming would rename a deployed resource and break the approval routing for no functional gain; the deck's identity is stated in this note instead.

ciso-global-pptx.notes: 9-slide Global CISO deck: contract owner, impacted ENX entities, service/supplier description, risk & controls resume, internal/external exposure diagram, ICT inherent+residual scores, ENX actions to the Contract Owner.

tpa-evidence-analysis.notes: Agent enumerates Infosec Assurance/GRC/TPA/Active/<Supplier> itself via read-only Graph tools; serviceName optional at trigger (d2): when absent the report is stored under Reports/<Supplier>/_ALL-SERVICES/ (serviceNameFallback) - a Logic App cannot ask; the orchestrator collects it conversationally when the user knows it.

soc-report-summary.notes: User-uploaded SOC 1/2/3 report -> full findings/exceptions/CUEC summary.

pentest-report-summary.notes: User-uploaded pentest report -> normalised findings register and reliance verdict.

ciso-exec-summary.notes: OneTrust Infosec Form PDF -> Strategic Risk Intelligence Dashboard (single-file HTML from assets/template.html, 5-domain spider, dual-perimeter). Extraction/classification/thresholds stay in the agent (verified JSON shown to the human first, as in ciso-reporting); the agent emits the finished HTML. Registered in templates/registry.json as ciso-executive-summary-html.

ai-deepsearch-report.notes: Second DeepSearch variant from the export (same 11 sections / dashboard contract as deepsearch-protocol). Kept as its own instance so results stay reproducible vs claude.ai.

cyber-forum-brief.notes: On-request structured THREAT-INTEL BRIEF (sections BLUF / DETAIL / ENX RELEVANCE / RECOMMENDATION / SOURCES) as DOCX. Vendor-advisory briefs are supplier-scoped (Reports/<Supplier>/<Service>/); non-vendor briefs land in Reports/General/Threat-Intel/. Verifier rule 1 lists the five sections (agents/verifier_instructions.md).

advisory-file-delivery.notes: Generic governed path for advisory deliverables (ISO 27001/42001, NIS2, DORA, EU AI Act, Form B drafts ...). agent = 'TRIGGER' means the caller passes agentId in the trigger body (the only instance that allows it). supplierName/serviceName are used as Advisory/<Framework-or-Topic>/<Subtopic>/ segments. Deploy one extra instance per renderFormat needed - docx via 'docx-generic', xlsx via 'xlsx-generic', pptx via 'pptx-generic' (the three generic house-style renderers; 'tprm-board-slide' is a specific board-slide template, not the generic pptx path) - files stay in chat only when the user does not ask to store them (agents/advisory_addendum.md). 'Living' documents are co-edited in Word/Excel Online from here (docs tool excluded).

transcript-summary.notes: Fed by workflows/speech-transcription.json (Azure AI Speech batch transcription + diarization, EU region). The workflow hands over the normalised `transcript` contract (templates/transcript.schema.json); the knowledge-only whisperx agent fills ONLY summary[], actions[] and notes[] and returns the contract otherwise unchanged, so every turn stays verbatim. renderTemplate was 'evidence-summary' until the dedicated renderer existed - it is now 'transcript', which emits md + html + docx from one payload (/api/render returns all three in files[]); the DOCX is the file of record under Reports/<Supplier>/<Service>/.

supplier-intake-triage.notes: Requirement k: the first lifecycle gate. Classifies supplier type, ICT-service criticality (DORA Art. 3(21)-(22) critical-or-important-function test), inherent risk profile and the assurance depth that follows, and names the follow-up systems to run (contract review, RoI entry, DPIA, EU AI Act screening). Tier A: it decides effort, not a commitment - the tiering itself is re-confirmed by the assessments it triggers.

contract-security-review.notes: Requirement l: clause-by-clause coverage of DORA Art. 30(2)/(3), Art. 29 subcontracting, GDPR Art. 28(3) + SCCs 2021/914, NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d), ENX security minimums, incident clocks, resilience and exit. Output feeds Legal/Procurement negotiation; the agent proposes wording and never states a legal conclusion. Tier B - it is read outside the team.

dora-register-of-information.notes: Requirement m: DORA Art. 28(3) Register of Information - one sheet per ITS table plus a Validation sheet listing every rule breach (missing mandatory field, bad LEI/ISO code, broken subcontracting rank chain, CIF service without RTO/RPO or exit plan). Supplier/Service segments are 'Register'/'<reporting reference date>' for a full-register run. Tier B: it is submitted by the accountable owner to the competent authority - the pipeline never submits.

concentration-risk-analysis.notes: Requirement n: DORA Art. 29 concentration risk plus the fourth-party chain - provider, fourth-party, geography, technology and entity dimensions, impact of failure against ENX recovery objectives, substitutability, and treatment options. Portfolio-scoped runs store under Reports/Portfolio/<scope>/. Tier B: concentration conclusions drive architecture and sourcing decisions.

continuous-monitoring-radar.notes: Requirement o: the standing ongoing-monitoring view between assessments (DORA Art. 28(1)(b), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.22) - evidence expiry, assessments due, external rating drift, overdue findings, expiring risk acceptances, undispositioned watch items. The agent emits the finished single-file HTML per agents/knowledge-packs/enx-html-design-guide.md with data-radar-asof on <body>; statuses are recomputed against the as-at date and never reused from the evidence cache. NOTE: SharePoint serves .html as a download, not inline - see sharepoint/README.md.

supplier-incident-assessment.notes: Requirement p: impact of a supplier incident on Euronext plus the notification-duty assessment with deadlines computed from the evidenced awareness timestamp (DORA Art. 18/19 major-incident classification, NIS2 Art. 23 24h/72h/1-month, GDPR Art. 33/34, contractual and client duties). The determination of record stays with CISO/DPO/Compliance/Legal - nothing here notifies anyone. Tier B and time-critical: the approval gate is the escalation, so route it to the senior approvers immediately.

exit-offboarding-assurance.notes: Requirement q: DORA Art. 28(8) exit strategy (PLAN mode - triggers, options, transition plan against the contractual transition period, data exit, continuity, test record, readiness verdict) or the evidenced offboarding checklist (OFFBOARD mode - access revocation, data return and certified deletion including subcontractors and backups, registers updated, surviving obligations). Mode is passed in the trigger body. Tier B.

findings-remediation-register.notes: Requirement r: the consolidated findings, remediation and risk-acceptance register - every finding from the evidence/SOC/pentest/DeepSearch/contract/concentration/incident systems normalised to one row with severity, control reference, owner, due date, status and closure evidence; every acceptance with expiry, authority and compensating controls. An expired acceptance reverts to OPEN. Portfolio runs store under Reports/Portfolio/Findings/. Tier A - it is the team's own working register.

isms-audit-pack.notes: Requirement s: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 governance packs for the third-party scope - SOA extract (cl. 6.1.3 / A.5.19-A.5.23), internal audit plan and report (cl. 9.2), management review input pack (cl. 9.3), or the audit evidence index for an external audit or supervisory request. Pack type is passed in the trigger body; supplierName/serviceName are the Advisory/<Pack-type>/<Scope>/ segments. Tier B: audit material leaves the team.

regulatory-change-watch.notes: Requirement t: regulatory and standards horizon scanning (DORA RTS/ITS, NIS2 transpositions, GDPR/EDPB, EU AI Act timeline, ISO/NIST/CIS/CSA/PCI/ISAE, ESA outsourcing guidelines) with, for each change, the ENX applicability, the named platform artefacts that must change, the gap assessment and an action plan worked backwards from the application date. Public official sources only - no ENX identifier ever enters a query. Tier A: it informs, and every change it proposes runs through its own change process.
